q: Gaboriau's theorem (2000) shows that free groups F_r and F_s (r≠s) have non-orbit-equivalent free ergodic actions because:
opts: Their ℓ²-Betti numbers differ: β₁^{(2)}(F_r) = r-1 ≠ s-1 = β₁^{(2)}(F_s), and ℓ²-Betti numbers are orbit-equivalence invariants
Their Cayley graphs are not isomorphic
exp: Gaboriau: β_n^{(2)}(R) = β_n^{(2)}(Γ) for free ergodic Γ-actions (ℓ²-Betti numbers of the relation = ℓ²-Betti numbers of the group). Since β₁^{(2)}(F_r)=r-1, free groups of different rank have non-OE free ergodic actions.
